Good—simple rules of thumb:

- Required proof or money/legal stuff → tuck away. (Tax docs, receipts you might need for returns, warranties, contracts.)
- Actionable items → keep in your inbox or snooze until done. Once done, delete unless you’ll need it for reference.
- One-off info you’ll never need again → delete. If you wouldn’t search for it later, it’s safe to go.
- Reference value → tuck away in a searchable folder/label. If it contains step-by-step instructions, policies, or contact details you’ll reuse, keep it.
- Attachments you want to keep → save the attachment to your drive and then delete the email (or tuck the email if you prefer the context).
- Subscriptions/newsletters → delete and unsubscribe if you don’t read them; otherwise auto-filter them out of the inbox into a folder.
- Sentimental but not useful → export/save elsewhere (notes/photos) then delete the email, or tuck away only what truly matters.

Quick note on terms: “Tuck away” = archive or move to a folder/label so it’s searchable and recoverable. “Delete” = remove to trash (eventually permanently gone). If you want, I can help apply these rules to specific messages — I will not delete anything until you confirm; I’ll first show exactly which messages would be affected and whether the action is reversible. Which approach do you want to start with (delete vs archive), and do you want a short time-based rule to use (e.g., delete unread after 90 days)?
